cards.q: Where does each tissue get the fatty acids for its TAG: liver vs adipose?
cards.a:
Liver: its own synthesis (major route)
Adipose: lipoproteins via LPL (little made there)
cards.more:
LiverAdipose
Glucose entryGLUT2GLUT4, insulin-dependent
Glycerol 3-P fromDHAP + free glycerolDHAP only
Fatty acids fromown synthesislipoproteins via LPL
TAGexported as VLDLstored

cards.q: Why does adipose tissue store little TAG when glucose or insulin is low?
cards.a: No glycerol kinase → glycerol 3-P only from DHAP → needs insulin-driven glucose entry via GLUT4

cards.q: What is the sequence of TAG synthesis from glycerol 3-phosphate, with enzymes?
cards.a: Glycerol 3-P → (GPAT) lysophosphatidic acid → (AGPAT) phosphatidic acid → (phosphatase) diacylglycerol → (DGAT) TAG
cards.more: GPAT = glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase; AGPAT = acylglycerol-phosphate acyltransferase; DGAT = diacylglycerol acyltransferase.

cards.q: How do insulin and AMPK regulate GPAT and MGAT?
cards.a:
Insulin activates (dephosphorylation)
AMPK inhibits
cards.more: MGAT = monoacylglycerol acyltransferase. Insulin also induces DGAT.

cards.q: Which TAG-synthesis enzyme does insulin induce?
cards.a: DGAT (diacylglycerol acyltransferase)

cards.q: What does AGPAT deficiency cause?
cards.a: Congenital generalised lipodystrophy: no adipose tissue + fatty liver

cards.q: Which TAG-synthesis enzyme is overexpressed in cancer, and which is studied as an obesity drug target?
cards.a:
Overexpressed in cancer: AGPAT
Obesity target: DGAT

cards.q: How does liver TAG reach peripheral tissues?
cards.a: As nascent VLDL, which matures in the blood

cards.q: What results when TAG builds up in the liver, and what is the clinical example?
cards.a: Fatty liver; alcoholic fatty liver (alcohol impairs VLDL export)

cards.q: What hormonal shift switches the body from storing to releasing fat?
cards.a: Insulin falls, glucagon rises

cards.q: Which adipose enzyme releases fatty acids from stored TAG during fasting?
cards.a: Hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL)

cards.q: What activates and what inhibits hormone-sensitive lipase?
cards.a:
Activated: glucagon, adrenaline (and cortisol)
Inhibited: insulin

cards.q: How are free fatty acids carried in the blood?
cards.a: Bound to albumin

cards.q: By what mechanism do glucagon and adrenaline activate hormone-sensitive lipase?
cards.a: ↑ cAMP → protein kinase → phosphorylates HSL (active)
cards.more: Insulin opposes this through a phosphatase.

cards.q: In what order is triacylglycerol taken apart during lipolysis?
cards.a: TAG → diacylglycerol → monoacylglycerol → glycerol + fatty acids

cards.q: Why can't adipocytes use the glycerol released by lipolysis?
cards.a: They lack glycerol kinase

cards.q: What happens to lipolysis glycerol in the liver?
cards.a: Glycerol kinase → glycerol 3-P → (glycerol 3-P dehydrogenase) DHAP → gluconeogenesis

cards.q: Where is fat burned, and in which tissues mainly?
cards.a: Mitochondrial matrix; liver and muscle

cards.q: Which cells do not oxidise fatty acids?
cards.a:
Brain
Cells without mitochondria (e.g. mature red cells)

cards.q: Which enzyme activates a fatty acid to fatty acyl-CoA, and where does it sit?
cards.a: Acyl-CoA synthetase; ER and outer mitochondrial and peroxisomal membranes

cards.q: What does fatty acid activation cost, and why that much?
cards.a: 2 ATP equivalents — ATP is split to AMP

cards.q: Which vitamin is coenzyme A made from?
cards.a: Vitamin B5

cards.q: Which fatty acids need the carnitine shuttle to enter the mitochondrion?
cards.a: Long chains (short and medium chains drift in)

cards.q: What are the three steps of the carnitine shuttle?
cards.a:
CPT-I (outer membrane): acyl-CoA → acylcarnitine
CACT: carries acylcarnitine in, swaps for free carnitine
CPT-II (inner membrane): acylcarnitine → acyl-CoA in matrix
cards.more: CPT = carnitine palmitoyltransferase; CACT = carnitine–acylcarnitine translocase.

cards.q: Where is CPT-I and what does it do?
cards.a: Outer mitochondrial membrane; moves acyl group from CoA to carnitine → acylcarnitine

cards.q: What does carnitine–acylcarnitine translocase (CACT) do?
cards.a: Carries acylcarnitine across the inner membrane in exchange for free carnitine

cards.q: Where is CPT-II and what does it do?
cards.a: Inner mitochondrial membrane; moves acyl group back onto CoA inside the matrix

cards.q: Where does carnitine come from?
cards.a: Mainly dietary meat; limited synthesis in liver and kidney from lysine and SAM
cards.more: SAM = S-adenosylmethionine.

cards.q: How do heart and skeletal muscle get carnitine?
cards.a: Cannot make it — high-affinity uptake transporter

cards.q: What is the rate-limiting step of fatty acid oxidation, and what inhibits it?
cards.a: CPT-I; malonyl-CoA

cards.q: Why can't a cell make fat and burn it at the same time?
cards.a: Malonyl-CoA (made only during fat synthesis) blocks CPT-I, so fatty acids cannot enter mitochondria
cards.more: The two pathways cannot run simultaneously and waste energy.

cards.q: How does low energy (high AMP) speed fatty acid oxidation?
cards.a: AMPK → inactivates ACC + promotes malonyl-CoA breakdown → CPT-I runs faster

cards.q: How do glucagon and adrenaline speed fatty acid oxidation?
cards.a: Inhibit ACC → malonyl-CoA falls → CPT-I faster

cards.q: How does insulin slow fatty acid oxidation?
cards.a: Stimulates ACC → malonyl-CoA rises → CPT-I slower

cards.q: When do fat synthesis vs breakdown run (insulin:glucagon)?
cards.a:
Synthesis: fed, high insulin:glucagon
Breakdown: starved, low insulin:glucagon

cards.q: Where do fat synthesis vs breakdown occur?
cards.a:
Synthesis: mainly liver; cytosol
Breakdown: muscle and liver; mitochondria

cards.q: What is the membrane carrier for fat synthesis vs breakdown?
cards.a:
Synthesis: citrate (out of mitochondria)
Breakdown: carnitine (into mitochondria)

cards.q: What is the chain carrier for fat synthesis vs breakdown?
cards.a:
Synthesis: acyl carrier protein, CoA
Breakdown: CoA

cards.q: What coenzymes do fat synthesis vs breakdown use?
cards.a:
Synthesis: NADPH (reduction)
Breakdown: NAD+, FAD (oxidation)

cards.q: How is the two-carbon unit handled in fat synthesis vs breakdown?
cards.a:
Synthesis: donated by malonyl-CoA
Breakdown: released as acetyl-CoA

cards.q: What is the key control of fat synthesis vs breakdown?
cards.a:
Synthesis: citrate activates ACC; long-chain acyl-CoA inhibits it
Breakdown: malonyl-CoA inhibits CPT-I

cards.q: What is the product of fat synthesis vs breakdown?
cards.a:
Synthesis: palmitate
Breakdown: acetyl-CoA
